subject: Sizing governor: token budget bands, per-service allocation and next checkpoints
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@sentryhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing governor: token budget bands, per-service allocation and next checkpoints

Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a proposed sizing + costing baseline so your procurement and engineering teams can budget the PoC. TL;DR: estimated blended target ~ $25–35 / 1M tokens; proposed monthly target budget (mid) ≈ $4k–$5k for the initial PoC traffic profile below.

What we heard on the call
- Target users: triage + clinician assistance (short prompts, lots of API calls), plus nightly embedding batch for search.
- Expected initial monthly volume (customer estimate): ~150M tokens/mo (this will scale).
- Quality mix: majority of interactions can use a quantized base chat model; ~10% require higher-fidelity context-aware generation; embeddings are frequent during search indexing and rerank ops are a smaller slice.

Proposed per-service split (initial PoC):
- Chat (generation): 60% -> 90M tokens/mo
  - Routing: ~90% of chat routed to 'base-quant' (low-latency, quantized) and ~10% to 'high-fidelity' for complex cases.
- Embeddings: 30% -> 45M tokens/mo
- Rerank / reranking pipelines: 10% -> 15M tokens/mo

Unit economics assumptions (ballpark estimates for budgeting):
- Chat (base-quant): $30 / 1M tokens
- Chat (high-fidelity): $120 / 1M tokens (applies to ~9M of the chat volume)
- Embeddings: $7 / 1M tokens
- Rerank: $18 / 1M tokens

Estimated monthly cost (based on above split)
- Chat base: 81M * $30 = $2,430
- Chat high-fidelity: 9M * $120 = $1,080
- Embeddings: 45M * $7 = $315
- Rerank: 15M * $18 = $270
- Blended monthly cost ≈ $4,095 (blended ≈ $27.3 / 1M tokens)

Recommended targets and asks for SentryHealth
1) Can you confirm the 150M/month is a reasonable mid PoC estimate (range min 50M – max 400M)?
2) Do you expect embedding generation to be batched (nightly) or near-real-time? (impacts instance sizing / latency SLOs)
3) Any compliance or data-retention quirks we should model now (PHI flagging, longer retention windows)?

Next steps (proposed)
- Vanessa: send PoC requirements + draft SLA (attached).
- SentryHealth: confirm budget band and procurement contact. If procurement is ready, we can spin up dedicated PoC capacity within 5–7 business days.
- Joint: 2-week PoC -> collection of representative traces, then optimization pass (batching & cache config) to hit <$30 / 1M target.

Attachments: SentryHealth_PoC_requirements.pdf (scope & acceptance), Redwood_SLA_Draft.docx

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Subject: Re: Sizing governor: token budget bands, per-service allocation and next checkpoints

Vanessa — thanks for the detailed breakdown, this is exactly what procurement and our infra lead needed to see. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 150M/month is a reasonable mid estimate for Phase 1. We expect a lower ramp (50–120M) for the first month as we warm up users, but please assume headroom to 400M in forecasts.
- Embeddings will be mostly batched nightly for indexing (good) but we do have a near-real-time stream for recent events (~10% of embedding volume).
- PHI: yes, some prompts contain PHI. We'll need to confirm the Private deployment options and KMS integration during procurement.

Procurement looped in (procurement@sentryhealth.com) — can you confirm next steps from your side for a draft SOW / PoC ordering? Also, when can Redwood provide an initial dedicated capacity quote for the 150M baseline?

Alex
Head of Product — Search & Knowledge, SentryHealth

- PHI / Private deployment: we can offer Redwood Private with KMS/HSM integration and audit log exports. I'll loop in our security lead if you want a SOC2 + architecture call.
- Embedding split: noted 90% batched / 10% streaming — we'll size ephemeral workers for the stream portion to keep costs low.

Action items
- Vanessa: share cleaned PoC scope + SLA (attached) — please confirm the acceptance criteria in section 3.
- Karthik: can you draft the dedicated PoC pricing ranges (low/mid/high) and put a small note about where we would apply quantized v. full-precision models?
- Alex / procurement: confirm procurement contact name and whether you prefer Redwood to send an initial commercial quote or a formal SOW first.

I propose a short procurement sync next Tue (Oct 5) — 30 minutes to review the pricing band and SOW approach. Are you available?

Thanks — Vanessa

Quick pricing ranges (draft) — putting these in the thread so procurement has numbers to work against for the Oct 5 sync. Final quote will be in formal doc.

Assumptions: 150M baseline, 30-day PoC, mixed routing described by Vanessa. Includes modest prefunding commit for dedicated option.

Option A — Hosted + Autoscale (no commit)
- Low (50M): ~$1.6k / month
- Mid (150M): ~$4.2k / month
- High (400M): ~$10.8k / month

Option B — Dedicated PoC fleet (1 month reserved capacity)
- Low: ~$1.3k / month (10–15% lower)
- Mid: ~$3.6k / month (applied discount; includes priority routing and fixed latency SLO)
- High: ~$9.2k / month

Notes
- Blended $/1M target for the mid PoC falls ~ $24–28 / 1M with dedup/kv-caching and quantized base routing applied aggressively.
- We recommend enabling prefix caching for clinician prompts and an embeddings cache to reduce repeated indexing calls during the PoC. Those levers materially reduce unit cost in month 2.

I'll prepare a short one-page commercial quote and bring it to the Tue sync. If procurement prefers, we can send the SOW + formal quote ahead of the meeting.

Karthik
Director, Solution Sales — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
